institution: Tsinghua University (School of Vehicle and Mobility)
primary: RL and optimal control for driving
summary: The lab develops reinforcement learning and optimal-control methods, such as distributional soft actor-critic variants, model-based and safe RL, and applies them to autonomous driving.
question: How can reinforcement learning be made reliable enough to serve as an optimal-control method for autonomous vehicles?

name: Intelligent Dynamics Lab (Roy Fox)
summary: Studies structure, exploration and optimization in deep RL, including world-model adaptation, delayed observations and self-play.
question: How do structure, exploration and optimization shape deep control learning in virtual and physical agents?

name: Intelligent Robot Lab (George Konidaris)
summary: Studies how agents learn skill and state abstraction hierarchies that support fast, goal-oriented planning, with applications to general-purpose robots.
question: How can an agent learn abstraction hierarchies that enable fast, goal-oriented planning?

name: Intelligent Robot Learning Lab, IRL Lab (Matthew E. Taylor)
summary: The lab does reinforcement learning research and applies it in simulated and physical settings, with a focus on human-in-the-loop RL, reward learning from human feedback and transfer.
question: How can reinforcement learning agents learn efficiently in real-world settings, including from human feedback?

name: Intelligent Robotics group (Ville Kyrki)
summary: The group develops learning methods for robots in unstructured environments, including reinforcement and imitation learning for manipulation, co-design and driving.
question: How can robots learn to operate reliably in unstructured environments built for humans?

name: Intelligent Space and Energy Systems (Günther Waxenegger-Wilfing)
summary: Studies reinforcement learning and planning for autonomous decision-making in safety-critical, data-scarce space and propulsion applications.
question: How can sequential decision-making algorithms let AI systems act autonomously and reliably in safety-critical, data-scarce environments?

name: Intelligent Systems and Robotics Lab (ISR Lab) (Jianyu Chen)
summary: The lab works at the intersection of AI and robotics, using reinforcement learning, control and learned world/video-prediction models for humanoid and manipulation robots.
question: How can reinforcement learning, robotics and control be combined to build robotic systems with high performance and high intelligence?

name: Intelligent Systems Lab (Ioannis Vlahavas)
summary: The lab applies deep reinforcement learning to autonomous driving, driver-assistance systems and game agents alongside AI planning research.
question: How can AI planning and learning techniques solve complex decision problems such as autonomous driving?

name: Intelligent Systems Laboratory (Jennie Si)
summary: The lab develops reinforcement learning and approximate dynamic programming for real-time control, including control of wearable robotic devices.
question: How can reinforcement learning control physical devices that interact with people in real time?

name: Intelligent Systems – multi-agent RL (Shihan Wang; Mehdi Dastani)
summary: Studies multi-agent deep RL, including communication, credit assignment, exploration and symbolic action masking.
question: How can complex agent-agent and human-agent interactions be modelled and integrated into reinforcement learning?

name: InterACT Lab (Anca Dragan)
summary: Develops algorithms for agents that learn what people want from interactive human feedback and assist humans, including RL post-training of LLM agents.
question: How can agents learn to do what people actually want through interaction and human feedback?

name: Interactive Intelligence – multi-objective and inverse RL (Luciano Cavalcante Siebert; Pradeep K. Murukannaiah)
lead: Luciano Cavalcante Siebert; Pradeep K. Murukannaiah
summary: Uses multi-objective and inverse RL to represent human values and intentions in autonomous systems, with applications such as water management and climate policy.
question: How can autonomous systems account for human values and intentions when they learn to act?

name: Interactive Learning and Decision Making (Frans Oliehoek)
summary: Works on decision making for agents that interact with complex worlds and other agents, including multi-agent RL, partially observable RL and game-theoretic learning.
question: How can an agent learn and decide well when it interacts with a complex world that includes other agents?

name: Interactive Robot Perception & Learning Lab – PEARL (Georgia Chalvatzaki)
summary: The lab studies robot learning for mobile manipulation, including diffusion-based maximum-entropy reinforcement learning and RL-driven data generation for bimanual dexterous manipulation.
question: How can robots acquire mobile manipulation skills through purposeful interaction so they can assist people in everyday tasks?

name: IRIS Lab (Chelsea Finn)
summary: Studies how robots and other agents acquire broadly capable behaviour through learning and interaction, including RL with expressive policies and real-robot RL.
question: How can robots and other agents develop broadly intelligent behaviour through learning and interaction?

name: Ishii Lab (Shin Ishii)
primary: RL and decision making in brains and machines
summary: The lab studies decision making with a focus on reinforcement learning, from multi-agent AI and robot control to links between machine RL and human brain activity.
question: How do learning machines and brains acquire decisions in complex, changing environments?

name: ISIR MLIA – Thome (Nicolas Thome)
summary: Works on sample-efficient model-based RL on real robots and on vision-language reward models and world models for embodied agents.
question: How can embodied agents learn useful world models and rewards from limited interaction?

name: ISIR – decision making in robots and animals (Mehdi Khamassi)
summary: Models decision making and RL in animals and robots, including model arbitration, curiosity-driven exploration and hippocampal replay.
question: How do animals and robots combine learning, reward and curiosity to make decisions?

name: ISIR – RL and developmental robotics (Olivier Sigaud; Nicolas Perrin-Gilbert; Stéphane Doncieux)
lead: Olivier Sigaud; Nicolas Perrin-Gilbert; Stéphane Doncieux
summary: Develops goal-conditioned, zero-shot and quality-diversity RL methods for robots and open-ended agents.
question: How can robots acquire diverse, reusable skills through reinforcement learning and exploration?

name: Ivana Dusparic (Trinity College Dublin)
summary: Dusparic's group develops reinforcement-learning methods, including multi-objective, constrained and model-based RL, for traffic control and other large-scale urban infrastructures.
question: How can AI, especially reinforcement learning, optimise resources in large-scale urban infrastructures such as transport systems?

name: Jana Tumova (KTH RPL)
summary: Tumova combines formal methods and temporal-logic specifications with planning and learning, including multi-agent and causal reinforcement learning for robots and vehicles.
question: How can formal specifications such as temporal logic guide safe planning, control and learning for robots and multi-agent systems?

name: Jason D. Lee group (Jason D. Lee)
summary: The group studies the theory of deep learning, reinforcement learning and preference-based fine-tuning of language models.
question: Why do reinforcement learning and preference optimisation work for training modern models?

name: Jeff Clune group (Jeff Clune)
institution: University of British Columbia; Vector Institute
summary: The group works on open-ended algorithms, AI-generating algorithms and self-improving agents, including foundation-model self-play and exploration methods descended from Go-Explore.
question: How can we create open-ended algorithms that keep innovating and learning forever?

name: Jeff Schneider group (Auton Lab)
summary: Works on reinforcement learning and decision making, including offline and model-based RL for tokamak plasma control, robotics and LLM agents.
question: How can agents learn reliable control policies from limited or offline data in high-stakes physical systems?

name: Jorge Mendez-Mendez group
summary: Studies embodied lifelong learning and compositional structure so that robots and RL agents accumulate and reuse knowledge over time.
question: How can embodied agents accumulate knowledge over their lifetimes to better interact with the world?

name: Jun Morimoto group (Jun Morimoto)
institution: Kyoto University (Graduate School of Informatics); ATR Computational Neuroscience Laboratories
primary: robot learning and RL for humanoids
summary: The group combines reinforcement learning, robotics and computational neuroscience for humanoid motor control and assistive robots, including zero-shot sim-to-real robot learning.
question: How can robots learn humanoid motor skills and assist human movement using learning methods informed by neuroscience?

name: Jun Wang (UCL Centre for Artificial Intelligence)
summary: Works on multi-agent RL, RL fine-tuning of LLM agents and generative models for decision making.
question: How can multi-agent RL and generative models be combined so that agents learn and adapt from experience?

name: Jun Zhang group (Jun Zhang)
institution: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (ECE)
primary: safe offline RL and world models
summary: The group works on safe offline reinforcement learning, multi-agent RL communication and world models, alongside edge AI systems.
question: How can agents learn safe and scalable policies from offline data and learned world models?

name: Junliang Xing group (Junliang Xing)
institution: Tsinghua University (Department of Computer Science and Technology)
summary: The group builds reinforcement-learning agents for adversarial and imperfect-information games (e.g. AlphaHoldem) and studies multi-task, offline and in-context RL and opponent modelling.
question: How can learning agents make strong decisions in adversarial games and other multi-agent settings?

name: Junxian He group (Junxian He)
institution: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (CSE)
summary: The group studies reinforcement learning for reasoning in large language models, including RL from verifiable rewards, reward models and agent training.
question: When and why does reinforcement learning improve the reasoning of language models?

name: Kaiqing Zhang group
primary: multi-agent RL and learning in games
summary: Studies multi-agent reinforcement learning and learning in games, including equilibrium computation and multi-agent training of language models.
question: How can multiple learning agents reach good outcomes when they interact strategically?

name: Karinne Ramirez-Amaro (Chalmers)
summary: Ramirez-Amaro's group combines symbolic models and planning with hierarchical reinforcement learning for long-horizon robot manipulation.
question: How can symbolic knowledge and planning make robot reinforcement learning work on long-horizon, multi-skill tasks?

name: Karl H. Johansson (KTH Decision and Control Systems)
summary: Johansson's group works on networked and distributed control and includes reinforcement-learning, inverse-RL and bandit-optimisation methods for vehicles and networked systems.
question: How can networked and distributed cyber-physical systems be controlled and estimated reliably, including through learning?

name: KAUST AI Initiative (Jürgen Schmidhuber)
institution: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST); IDSIA
summary: The group works on artificial curiosity, upside-down reinforcement learning, world models and meta-learning, and applies curiosity-driven planning and RL to LLM-based agents.
question: How can agents learn to explore and improve themselves through curiosity and compression progress?

name: Keen Technologies (John Carmack)
summary: Researches RL agents that learn online from streams of experience, including the Physical Atari platform for real-time RL on robots.
question: How can agents learn efficiently online from real-time streams of experience rather than static datasets?

name: Kevin Jamieson group
summary: Develops bandit, active-learning and online-RL algorithms with provable guarantees for adaptive data collection.
question: How should a learner adaptively choose which data to collect?

name: Khimya Khetarpal (Google DeepMind Montreal)
summary: Works on how RL agents represent world knowledge through affordances and self-predictive representations, plan with temporal abstractions, and adapt over time.
question: How can agents efficiently represent the world's knowledge, plan with it, and adapt to changes over time through interaction?

name: Kianté Brantley group
primary: RL and imitation for foundation models
summary: Studies reinforcement learning and imitation learning methods that improve the decision-making of foundation models from interactive feedback.
question: How can learning from interactive feedback correct misalignment in systems built on foundation models?

name: Kim G. Larsen (Aalborg, DEIS)
summary: Larsen's group combines model checking and strategy synthesis with reinforcement learning, building shields that keep learning agents safe.
question: How can verification and synthesis produce safe, secure and optimal strategies for cyber-physical systems, including learned ones?

name: Kimberly Stachenfeld (Google DeepMind NYC)
primary: RL and predictive maps in brains
summary: Studies how brains build predictive models of the world, linking RL concepts such as the successor representation and dopamine-mediated reinforcement to behaviour and to machine learning models.
question: How do brains build models of the world that support memory and prediction, and how can these functions be implemented in learning systems?

name: Kimin Lee group (Kimin Lee)
primary: RL from human feedback and robot RL
summary: The group works on robot learning, reinforcement learning (including offline RL and RL from human feedback) and AI alignment.
question: How can agents and robots learn behaviour that is aligned with human intent from feedback and data?

name: Knowledge Technology (Stefan Wermter)
summary: The group develops neuroscience-inspired learning agents and robots, including RL from AI feedback and agentic skill discovery with reinforcement learning.
question: How can nature-inspired hybrid neural and symbolic representations yield continually learning robots and agents with vision and language?

name: Kwang-Sung Jun group (Kwang-Sung Jun)
primary: bandits and pure exploration in RL
summary: The group studies interactive machine learning, including bandits, pure exploration in RL and on-policy preference learning, with new confidence bounds.
question: How can interactive learners use confidence bounds to explore efficiently?

name: LAAS-CNRS Gepetto (Nicolas Mansard)
summary: Combines trajectory optimization and differentiable models with RL to control humanoid and legged robots.
question: How can anthropomorphic robots generate and control complex movement, using both optimal control and learning?

name: Laboratory for Artificial Intelligence and Learning Algorithms – LAILA (Nicolò Cesa-Bianchi)
summary: The lab studies the foundations of learning algorithms, proving regret bounds for bandits, online learning and reinforcement-learning settings with delayed or partial feedback.
question: What are the foundations of learning algorithms for sequential decision making, from online learning and bandits to reinforcement learning?

name: Laboratory for Information and Inference Systems – LIONS (Volkan Cevher)
summary: Develops provably efficient algorithms for imitation learning, value-based RL, preference-based alignment and multi-agent learning.
question: How can mathematical theory and computational methods learn efficiently from incomplete data, including interaction, demonstrations and preferences?

name: Laboratory of Computational Neuroscience (Wulfram Gerstner)
summary: Models how reward, novelty and surprise act as third factors in synaptic plasticity and drive exploration in humans and neural networks.
question: How do neuromodulatory signals such as reward, novelty and surprise gate learning in neural circuits?

name: Laboratory of Neural Computation and Cognition (Michael J. Frank)
institution: Brown University (Carney Institute for Brain Science)
summary: The lab builds neural-circuit and algorithmic models of basal ganglia–cortex interactions underlying reinforcement learning, decision making and cognitive control, and tests them with experiments.
question: What neural mechanisms underlie reinforcement learning, decision making and cognitive control?

name: Laixi Shi group (Laixi Shi)
institution: Johns Hopkins University (Electrical and Computer Engineering)
summary: The group develops robust and multi-agent reinforcement learning with sample-efficiency guarantees and studies safe sim-to-real transfer.
question: How can reinforcement learning be made robust, safe and sample-efficient in multi-agent and real-world settings?

name: Lak Lab (Armin Lak)
summary: Studies how dopamine and striatal circuits implement reward- and sensory-prediction-error learning in mice, linking signals to deep-network and RL models.
question: What neuronal circuit mechanisms underlie learning and decision-making?

name: LAMDA reinforcement learning group (Yang Yu)
summary: The group develops model-based, offline and multi-agent RL methods, including world-model-based policy optimization for vision-language-action agents.
question: How can learned environment models make reinforcement learning sample-efficient enough for real-world decision-making?

name: Language, Reasoning and Education Lab (Mrinmaya Sachan)
primary: rl for llm reasoning and tutoring
summary: Uses RL, including multi-turn RL, to train language models for reasoning and to align them with pedagogical goals in tutoring.
question: How can language models reason reliably and be aligned to teach well rather than only solve problems?

name: Latent Learning Lab (Nicolas W. Schuck)
summary: The lab combines behavioural and neuroimaging studies with reinforcement-learning-inspired models to study how the brain forms task state representations and uses replay for learning and decisions.
question: How does the brain build the representation of the current task state that reinforcement learning needs, and how does replay shape it?

name: Learning & Adaptive Systems Group (Andreas Krause)
summary: Develops RL and sequential decision-making methods that use uncertainty estimates for safe exploration, model-based control and data-efficient learning on real robots.
question: How can learning systems actively acquire information, reason and make reliable decisions in complex, uncertain domains?

name: Learning & Intelligent Systems Group (Leslie Kaelbling; Tomás Lozano-Pérez)
summary: Combines reinforcement learning, model learning and task-and-motion planning to build robots that act under uncertainty in unstructured environments.
question: What principles let robots with imperfect sensors and incomplete knowledge perform everyday tasks?

name: Learning Agents Research Group (LARG) (Peter Stone)
institution: University of Texas at Austin; Sony AI
summary: Studies how to create complete intelligent agents through machine learning, especially reinforcement learning, multiagent systems and robotics.
question: How can we best create complete intelligent agents that adapt, interact and are embodied?

name: Learning and Dynamical Systems Group (Michael Muehlebach)
institution: Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems
summary: The group combines machine learning, dynamical systems and control theory, including model-based and partially observable reinforcement learning for robot control.
question: How can a-priori known structure of physical systems make learning-based control more sample-efficient and generalisable?

name: Learning and Intelligent Systems Lab (Marc Toussaint)
summary: The lab bridges AI reasoning, optimisation and machine learning for robotics, including combining constrained sampling-based planning with reinforcement learning for manipulation.
question: How does the interplay of learning and reasoning, of data-based and model-based decision making, yield strongly generalising robot intelligence?

name: Learning and Interactive Robots – LaIR (Jens Kober)
summary: Develops RL and interactive imitation learning for robot motor skills, including guided exploration and hierarchical RL.
question: How can robots learn motor skills efficiently from their own experience and from human feedback?

name: Learning and Optimization Group (Zhihua Zhang)
summary: The group applies statistical inference, optimisation and stochastic analysis to machine learning, including finite-sample analysis of distributional TD learning and convergence of policy gradient methods.
question: What statistical and optimisation principles explain how learning algorithms, including reinforcement learning, work?

name: Learning in Neural Circuits Lab – LiNC (Blake Richards)
summary: The lab studies learning in neural circuits and brain-inspired deep learning, including continual reinforcement learning with fast and slow successor features and eligibility-trace credit assignment.
question: How do neural circuits learn, and what can deep learning and reinforcement learning reveal about learning in the brain?

name: Learning Systems and Robotics Lab (Angela Schoellig)
summary: Combines control, machine learning and optimization for safe learning-based robot control, including safety-filtered RL and GPU-accelerated drone simulators for policy learning.
question: How can robots in unstructured, changing environments learn while keeping guarantees on safety, performance and reliability?

name: Learning Technical Systems (Setareh Maghsudi)
summary: The chair studies decision-making under uncertainty with bandit algorithms and multi-agent reinforcement learning for networked engineering systems.
question: How can networked multi-agent systems make good decisions under uncertainty in engineering settings such as IoT and energy management?

name: Learning, Embodied Autonomy, and Forecasting Lab, LEAF (Nicholas Rhinehart)
summary: The lab works on general-purpose model-based control by combining learned world models (forecasting) with learned objectives (reward learning), including preference-based RL.
question: How can autonomous systems combine accurate world models with learned objectives to perform a wide range of tasks?

name: LeCAR Lab (Guanya Shi)
summary: Develops learning and control methods, including reinforcement learning combined with model-based control, for agile humanoids and other generalist robots.
question: How can learning and control be combined to make generalist robots reliable, adaptive and agile?

name: Lee Wee Sun group (Wee Sun Lee)
institution: National University of Singapore (Department of Computer Science)
summary: The group studies machine learning and planning under uncertainty, including RL algorithms for language models and RL for latent planning.
question: How can agents plan and learn effectively under uncertainty?

name: Levi Lelis group (Levi H. S. Lelis)
summary: The group develops combinatorial search algorithms for finding programmatic representations, such as computer programs encoding policies and options, for sequential decision-making problems.
question: How can search find programmatic representations, such as programs encoding policies, that solve reinforcement learning problems?

name: Lin F. Yang group
summary: Develops fast RL and decision-making algorithms with provable guarantees, including sample complexity of constrained MDPs.
question: How can decision-making algorithms be made fast, safe and provably efficient under uncertainty?

name: Lin Zhao group (Lin Zhao)
institution: National University of Singapore (Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering)
primary: actor-critic theory and RL for control
summary: The group combines control theory, optimisation and machine learning, with a focus on analysing actor-critic algorithms, offline RL and learning-based control of unmanned aerial vehicles.
question: How can reinforcement learning algorithms be designed to train efficiently and control systems with theoretical guarantees?

name: Ling Pan group (Ling Pan)
institution: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Department of Electronic and Computer Engineering)
summary: The group works on the theory, algorithms and applications of deep reinforcement learning, GFlowNets and multi-agent systems, including network plasticity in deep RL and RL for language-model post-training.
question: How can deep reinforcement learning and multi-agent decision-making algorithms be made robust, efficient and practical?

name: Lingzhou Xue group (Lingzhou Xue)
summary: The group studies statistical theory for reinforcement learning, including gap-dependent regret for Q-learning and federated Q-learning.
question: How can model-free reinforcement learning achieve optimal regret with low communication and switching cost?

name: Lira Lab (Erdem Bıyık)
primary: learning from human feedback for robots
summary: Develops RL and reward-learning methods that use human preferences and demonstrations for robot learning and human-robot interaction.
question: How can robots learn efficiently and safely from diverse forms of human feedback?

name: LIRIS – Matignon (Laëtitia Matignon)
summary: Works on deep multi-agent RL, exploration and transfer with behavioral foundation models, and socially compliant robot navigation.
question: How can multiple learning agents coordinate and transfer what they have learned?

name: LiVe Lab – Learning in Verification (Jan Křetínský)
summary: Combines machine learning and verification, including multi-task RL from LTL instructions, robustness certification of RL policies and risk-aware decision-making.
question: How can learning and formal verification be combined to obtain controllers that are both efficient and trustworthy?

name: LOCA Lab (Aditya Gopalan)
institution: Indian Institute of Science (Department of Electrical Communication Engineering)
summary: The lab studies learning and inference for sequential decisions, including bandits, policy iteration methods and uncertainty-aware RLHF.
question: How can learning algorithms make reliable sequential decisions under uncertainty?

name: Loewenstein Lab (Yonatan Loewenstein)
institution: Hebrew University of Jerusalem (Edmond and Lily Safra Center for Brain Sciences)
primary: RL in the brain and behaviour
summary: The lab studies the neural mechanisms and computational principles of learning, including operant learning, quantitative RL models of choice and whether value representations are needed to explain behaviour.
question: What computational principles and neural mechanisms underlie operant learning, and can choices be engineered using quantitative reinforcement learning models?

name: Long Tran-Thanh (University of Warwick)
summary: Develops online-learning and RL methods with guarantees for systems of collaborating or competing agents.
question: What mathematical foundations allow large systems of autonomous agents to collaborate or act strategically against each other?

name: Lucchi Group (Aurelien Lucchi)
summary: Studies RL-based post-training of language models for reasoning, including curricula at the edge of model capability and multi-task GRPO.
question: How can optimization and RL post-training make language-model reasoning reliable across tasks?

name: Lygeros Group, Automatic Control Laboratory (John Lygeros)
summary: Develops large-scale solvers and theory for Markov decision processes, including risk-averse MDPs, and applies deep RL to scheduling problems.
question: How can large-scale and risk-averse sequential decision problems be solved efficiently and reliably?

name: Machine Intelligence Lab (MiLAB) (Donglin Wang)
summary: The lab researches deep RL theory, meta-learning and robot behaviour learning so that real robots can adapt quickly and learn autonomously.
question: How can reinforcement learning and meta-learning give real robots behavioural flexibility, fast adaptation and autonomous learning?

name: Machine Intelligence through Decision-making and Interaction (MIDI) Lab (Amy Zhang)
summary: Develops theory and algorithms for reinforcement learning, with a focus on representations that improve generalization, robustness and sample efficiency.
question: How can reinforcement learning algorithms generalize and adapt for sequential decision-making in the real world?

name: Machine Learning and Intelligent Control Lab (Seungyul Han)
institution: UNIST (Artificial Intelligence Graduate School; Department of Electrical Engineering)
summary: The lab develops multi-agent, robust and offline RL methods, including cross-domain offline RL and zero-shot coordination.
question: How can reinforcement learning agents coordinate and transfer robustly across agents and domains?

name: Machine Learning and Mind Lab (MLML) (Sungjin Ahn)
institution: KAIST (School of Computing; KAIST-Mila Prefrontal AI Research Center); New York University
primary: world models and planning for agents
summary: The lab studies world models, model-based planning and open-ended embodied agents as foundations for decision-making systems.
question: How can agents learn compositional world models of their environment and use them to plan?

name: Machine Learning and Positioning Systems Lab (Christopher Mutschler)
summary: Develops constrained and risk-aware reinforcement learning methods with safety and stability guarantees aimed at deployment in safety-critical systems.
question: How can reinforcement learning be made safe, stable and explainable enough for safety-critical deployment?

name: Machine Learning Group – Lenaerts (Tom Lenaerts)
summary: Studies cooperation in multi-agent RL, including task generation that requires cooperation and the role of unrewarded subgoals.
question: How do cooperation and collective behavior emerge and get learned in groups of agents?

name: Machine Teaching Group (Adish Singla)
institution: Max Planck Institute for Software Systems
summary: The group studies machine teaching, including curriculum design for RL agents, policy teaching and RL from human feedback, with applications in education.
question: How can AI systems teach and be taught effectively, for example through curriculum design for learning agents?

name: Marek Cygan
summary: Works on scaling and regularizing value functions for sample-efficient and multi-task continuous-control RL, with links to robotic manipulation.
question: How can value-based RL scale model capacity to become compute- and sample-efficient across many tasks?

name: Marek Petrik group (Marek Petrik)
summary: The group develops robust and risk-averse reinforcement learning and dynamic programming methods that account for model uncertainty.
question: How can decisions learned from limited data remain reliable under model uncertainty and risk?

name: Mark Crowley group (Mark Crowley)
summary: The group studies decision making for single and multiple agents, including how ethical or moral requirements change the definition of reinforcement learning.
question: How do the structure and challenges of ethical or moral requirements affect how we define learning and decision making?

name: Marlos C. Machado group (Marlos C. Machado)
primary: representation learning and options in RL
summary: The group studies representation learning, temporally-extended exploration with options, Laplacian/successor-style representations and continual RL.
question: How can agents learn representations and temporally-extended behaviours (options) that support exploration, planning and continual learning?

name: Marquardt Division (Florian Marquardt)
institution: Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light
summary: Uses reinforcement learning to discover control strategies and circuits for quantum devices, as part of work on machine learning for physics.
question: Can machine learning act like a scientist and discover new strategies for controlling quantum devices?

name: Martha White group (Martha White)
summary: The group develops prediction and control algorithms that learn and adapt during deployment, with empirical studies of actor-critic and value-based methods and applications to industrial control such as water treatment.
question: How can prediction and control systems learn and adapt reliably during deployment in the real world?

name: Masset Lab (Paul Masset)
summary: The lab models how heterogeneous neuron types support distributed computations such as dopamine-based distributional and multi-horizon reinforcement learning, and tests these models experimentally.
question: How could dopamine-based distributed reinforcement learning be implemented in brain circuits?

name: Mathis Group (Alexander Mathis)
summary: Uses deep RL and imitation learning to train controllers for musculoskeletal models of human and animal bodies and relates them to motor neuroscience.
question: How do brains acquire adaptive motor skills, and can RL agents controlling realistic musculoskeletal bodies help explain this?

name: Matsuo-Iwasawa Laboratory (Yutaka Matsuo)
summary: The lab studies deep learning, world models and reinforcement learning, including constrained MDP theory, exploration in policy gradients and RL for language models.
question: How can agents acquire world models and decision-making abilities through deep learning?

name: Mattar Lab (Marcelo Mattar)
primary: planning and replay in the brain
summary: The lab uses experiments and reinforcement-learning models to study how the brain simulates the future to guide decisions, including planning, replay and memory sampling.
question: How does the brain simulate the future to guide decisions?

name: Matteo Leonetti (King's College London)
summary: Works on hierarchical RL with abstractions and on combining RL with planning for autonomous robots and teamwork.
question: How can reinforcement learning be combined with planning and reasoning for autonomous robots?

name: Max Simchowitz group (Max Simchowitz)
summary: The group studies the theory and practice of imitation learning and RL fine-tuning of generative control policies for robotics.
question: When and why do imitation learning and RL fine-tuning of generative policies succeed in control?

name: Medical Computing Laboratory (Tze-Yun Leong)
institution: National University of Singapore (School of Computing)
summary: The lab works on decision-theoretic AI, including reward shaping and knowledge transfer in multi-task reinforcement learning, alongside biomedical and health informatics.
question: How can agents share and transfer knowledge to learn decisions efficiently across tasks?

name: Mengdi Wang group (Mengdi Wang)
summary: The group works on reinforcement learning theory and RL frameworks for training language and diffusion models, with applications in science and engineering design.
question: How can reinforcement learning make generative models reliable optimisers for scientific and engineering goals?

name: Meta FAIR Paris – Behavioural foundation models / zero-shot RL (Alessandro Lazaric)
primary: zero-shot rl and behavioural foundation models
summary: Builds behavioural foundation models pre-trained without task rewards, such as Meta Motivo for humanoid control, and studies representations and jumpy world models for zero-shot RL and planning.
question: Can a single behavioural foundation model, pre-trained without rewards, solve new control tasks zero-shot at inference time?

name: Meta FAIR Paris – Rémi Munos
summary: Works on RL theory and on RL methods for language-model reasoning, such as trained search policies that steer exploration and RL-based post-training for Lean theorem proving.
question: Can exploration in language-model reasoning be steered by learned search policies instead of naive repeated sampling?

name: Michael Bowling group (Michael Bowling)
summary: The group studies how agents learn through experience, with work on imperfect-information games such as poker, multi-agent learning, exploration and monitored MDPs.
question: How can computers learn to act and play games well through experience?

name: Michael Littman group
summary: Works on reinforcement learning and its interaction with people, including continual model-based RL and interfaces that let non-experts specify RL tasks for robots.
question: How can people specify and benefit from reinforcement learning agents?

name: Michiel van de Panne group (Michiel van de Panne)
summary: The group uses deep reinforcement learning for agile human motion, legged locomotion, physics-based character animation and robot control.
question: How can simulated characters and robots learn agile, skilful motion?

name: Micro Air Vehicle Lab – MAVLab (Guido de Croon)
summary: Trains end-to-end and model-based RL controllers for small drones, including vision-based racing and sim-to-real transfer of depth perception.
question: How can tiny drones fly autonomously with very limited onboard sensing and computation?

name: Microsoft Research AI for Science – Elise van der Pol
summary: Studies symmetry and structure in deep RL, including expected-return symmetries for coordination and group-structured world models.
question: How can symmetry and structure make deep RL more efficient and useful for science?

name: Microsoft Research NYC Reinforcement Learning Group (Akshay Krishnamurthy; Dylan Foster)
summary: Develops statistical and computational foundations for RL, bandits and imitation learning, and applies them to pre-training, post-training and exploration in language models.
question: What are the statistical and computational foundations of learning from interaction and feedback over time?

name: Milan Češka
summary: Uses deep reinforcement learning together with formal synthesis to compute finite-state controllers for (hidden-model) POMDPs.
question: How can deep RL scale the synthesis of robust controllers for partially observable systems?

name: Min-hwan Oh group (Min-hwan Oh)
institution: Seoul National University (Graduate School of Data Science)
summary: The group designs and analyses algorithms for sequential decision making, including contextual bandits, offline and preference-based reinforcement learning, with regret and sample-complexity guarantees.
question: How can sequential decision-making algorithms for bandits and reinforcement learning be made both statistically optimal and practical?

name: Ming Jin group (Ming Jin)
summary: The group works on safe and robust reinforcement learning, including constrained offline RL and robustness benchmarks, and on AI safety.
question: How can learning-based decision systems remain safe under uncertainty and human irrationality?

name: Mingfei Sun (University of Manchester)
summary: Works on policy-gradient methods, credit assignment in multi-agent RL and learning from demonstration.
question: How can deep RL and learning from demonstration be made efficient for games, robotics and multi-agent systems?

name: MIRA Lab (Jie Wang)
institution: University of Science and Technology of China
primary: deep RL and learning to optimize
summary: MIRA Lab works on deep reinforcement learning and representation learning, including RL for combinatorial optimisation, chip design and language-model reasoning.
question: How can reinforcement learning solve complex decision and optimisation problems in science and engineering?

name: Mirco Musolesi (UCL)
summary: Studies multi-agent RL from a dynamical-systems perspective, distributional RL in chaotic systems and cooperation among LLM agents.
question: How do learning agents, including language-model agents, cooperate and compete in multi-agent systems?

name: Mobile and Distributed Systems Group (Claudia Linnhoff-Popien)
summary: Studies multi-agent reinforcement learning, including peer incentivization for cooperation and interpretable RL, alongside quantum computing methods.
question: How can autonomous systems be built with methods from AI and quantum computing?

name: Moonshot AI Kimi Team (Yang Zhilin)
summary: Trains the Kimi language models with large-scale reinforcement learning for long-context reasoning and agentic tasks.
question: How can reinforcement learning be scaled to train language models for long-horizon reasoning and agentic use?

name: Motivation, Brain and Behaviour team – MBB (Mathias Pessiglione)
summary: Studies how the brain represents costs and benefits in decisions, including computational models of reward learning in patients and drug effects.
question: How are costs and benefits represented in the brain, and how is this trade-off biased by emotion, fatigue and disease?

name: Muhammad Burhan Hafez (University of Southampton)
summary: Studies continual robot motor learning with intrinsic motivation, world models and combined model-based and model-free control.
question: How can robots efficiently and continually acquire new skills using intrinsic motivation and adaptive integration of model-based and model-free control?

name: Multi-agent Networks Laboratory (Minghui Zhu)
summary: The lab studies distributed decision making for multi-agent networks, including safe meta-reinforcement learning, explainable RL and RL from human feedback.
question: How can learning agents adapt quickly and safely while explaining their decisions?

name: Multi-Agent Systems Group (Goran Radanovic)
institution: Max Planck Institute for Software Systems
summary: The group studies the robustness and accountability of reinforcement learning, including corruption-robust offline RL and distributionally robust RL from human feedback.
question: How should AI systems with multiple, possibly self-interested agents be designed and analysed to be robust and accountable?

name: Multiagent Systems group – value-aligned RL (Juan A. Rodríguez-Aguilar)
summary: The group designs multi-agent reinforcement-learning environments and multi-objective RL methods that provably incentivise agents to behave in line with ethical values.
question: How can multi-agent systems, including learning agents, be built to act in line with the ethical and social values of the people who use them?

name: Multimodal and Embodied Reasoning group (Manling Li)
summary: The group trains language and vision-language agents with multi-turn reinforcement learning and studies world-model reasoning for embodied agents.
question: How can multimodal agents learn to reason and act over many turns through reinforcement learning?

name: Na Li group
primary: control and RL for dynamical systems
summary: Studies the interplay of control and learning, including model-based and model-free reinforcement learning and scalable multi-agent learning for physical systems.
question: How can control theory and reinforcement learning be combined for scalable, reliable decision making in dynamical systems?

name: Namboodiri Lab (Vijay Mohan K. Namboodiri)
summary: The lab studies the biological algorithms behind associative learning and decision making, testing retrospective causal-learning accounts of dopamine against temporal-difference RL.
question: What biological algorithms and network mechanisms underlie associative learning, memory and decision making?

name: Nan Jiang group
summary: Builds the theoretical foundations of reinforcement learning in the function-approximation setting, including off-policy evaluation and offline RL.
question: When and how can reinforcement learning with function approximation be statistically efficient?

name: Nathan Kallus group (Nathan Kallus)
summary: The group works on causal inference and off-policy reinforcement learning, including risk-sensitive and distributional RL and RL for recommender systems.
question: How can we learn and evaluate decision policies reliably from observational data?

name: Naver Labs Europe – Spatial AI (Christian Wolf)
summary: Industry research on embodied agents trained with RL for visual and social navigation, including memory architectures.
question: How can robots learn high-level reasoning and navigation skills from visual observations?

name: Ness Shroff group (Ness Shroff)
summary: The group develops reinforcement learning with safety constraints and multiple objectives, with theory for linear MDPs and applications in networked systems.
question: How can reinforcement learning agents explore efficiently while respecting safety constraints?

name: Network Control Laboratory (Francesco Delli Priscoli)
summary: The lab applies deep and multi-agent reinforcement learning to control problems such as vehicle platooning, insulin dosing, medical imaging and space debris capture.
question: How can multi-agent learning techniques control and manage complex networked systems in health, energy, transport and communications?

name: Neural & Machine Learning Group (Rui Ponte Costa)
summary: Combines neuroscience and machine learning to study learning in the brain, including hippocampal models of multi-task RL under partial observability.
question: What principles underlie learning in the brain?

name: Neural Computation Unit (Kenji Doya)
institution: Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology (OIST)
summary: The unit combines theory, neuroscience experiments and robots to study how biological and artificial agents learn behaviours by exploration and reward.
question: How can a biological or artificial agent learn novel behaviours in uncertain environments by exploration and reward feedback?

name: Neuro-Cognitive Modeling Group (Martin V. Butz)
summary: The group develops event-predictive cognitive models and contextual reinforcement learning methods, including framing causal discovery as an RL problem.
question: How does the brain learn and maintain context-conditioned, event-predictive structures that generate and control attention, thought and behaviour?

name: Neurorobotics Lab (Joschka Boedecker)
summary: The lab develops data-efficient deep reinforcement learning methods built on Q-learning for robotics, autonomous driving and neurotechnology.
question: How can deep reinforcement learning give robust, sample-efficient and adaptive decision policies for real-world robots and devices?

name: Nicola Gatti (Politecnico di Milano)
primary: online learning in games and markets
summary: Gatti works at the intersection of game theory and learning, proving regret guarantees for constrained MDPs, bandits and online learning in economic settings.
question: How can online learning minimise regret in equilibrium and economic problems such as auctions and constrained decision processes?

name: Niv Lab (Yael Niv)
primary: RL and representation learning in the brain
summary: The lab builds computational models of how experience changes future choices, focusing on representation learning for RL and its application to mental-health conditions.
question: How does experience change future decisions, and how can computational models of learning inform the treatment of mental-health conditions?

name: NVIDIA GEAR Lab (Jim Fan; Yuke Zhu)
summary: Builds generalist embodied agents and humanoid foundation models (GR00T) and uses sim-to-real RL for vision-based dexterous humanoid manipulation.
question: How can generalist embodied agents be built that act across virtual worlds and physical humanoid robots?

name: NVIDIA Seattle Robotics Lab (Yashraj Narang)
summary: Develops simulation-based robot learning methods, including RL with kinesthetic teaching and simulation-in-the-loop sim-to-real transfer for contact-rich manipulation.
question: How can simulation and learning be combined so robots acquire contact-rich manipulation skills that transfer to the real world?

name: Oak Lab (Richard S. Sutton; Khurram Javed)
summary: Builds the OaK architecture for agents that learn continually from experience with batch-size-one, replay-free algorithms and plan with learned temporal abstractions.
question: How can agents discover and implement algorithms to achieve goals in big worlds by learning directly from experience?

name: OpenAI RL & Reasoning (Jakub Pachocki)
summary: Trains the o-series reasoning models with large-scale reinforcement learning and has published on RL for competitive programming and on monitoring RL-trained reasoning models.
question: How far can scaling general-purpose reinforcement learning take language models on reasoning tasks?

name: Openmind Research Institute (Joseph Modayil; Richard S. Sutton)
summary: A Canadian non-profit institute that funds research fellows and publishes open-source basic research following the Alberta Plan, including real-time RL robot platforms and streaming/differential TD methods.
question: How can minds form from computation interacting with a general continuing data stream and learn in real time from sensorimotor experience?

name: Optimization & Decision Intelligence Group (Niao He)
summary: Analyses RL, constrained exploration, RLHF and learning in mean-field games through optimization and learning theory.
question: How can optimization and learning theory yield provably efficient and trustworthy automated decision-making?

name: Optimization and Statistical Inference Lab (OSI Lab) (Se-Young Yun)
institution: KAIST (Kim Jaechul Graduate School of AI)
primary: RL theory and RL for LLMs
summary: The lab works on problems from RL theory and bandits to RL-based alignment and reasoning for language models.
question: How can provably efficient learning and RL methods improve decision-making and alignment in generative models?

name: Oxford Control and Verification – OXCAV (Alessandro Abate)
summary: Combines formal verification and control of stochastic systems with RL to synthesise certified policies, including LTL-guided multi-task RL.
question: How can sequential decision making for complex dynamical models, built from first principles or learnt from data, be made safe and certified?

name: Pablo Samuel Castro (Google DeepMind Montreal)
institution: Google DeepMind; Université de Montréal (adjunct); Mila
summary: Studies the training dynamics, scaling and evaluation of deep RL agents, including gradient stability and representation learning for multitask deep RL.
question: What makes deep reinforcement learning networks train stably and scale with more parameters and tasks?

name: Pan Xu Lab (Pan Xu)
summary: The lab works on statistical and algorithmic foundations of reinforcement learning, with recent focus on distributionally robust MDPs and off-dynamics offline RL.
question: How can agents learn decision policies that transfer reliably across shifts in environment dynamics?

name: Paria Rashidinejad group (Paria Rashidinejad)
primary: offline RL and RL for LLMs
summary: The group studies offline reinforcement learning and RL methods for reasoning in language and diffusion language models.
question: How can reinforcement learning extract the most from fixed data and expensive compute?

name: Pascal Poupart group (Pascal Poupart)
summary: The group works on sequential decision making under uncertainty, including multi-agent RL, inverse constrained RL and Bayesian model-based planning.
question: How can agents make good sequential decisions under uncertainty, alone and with other agents?

name: Paton Lab (Joseph Paton)
summary: The lab records and manipulates neural activity in behaving rodents to study how dopamine and basal-ganglia circuits implement temporal-difference and distributional learning of future reward over time.
question: How do animals learn which cues predict behaviourally important events, treating credit assignment as inference in the time domain?

name: Patrick M. Pilarski group (Patrick M. Pilarski)
summary: The group applies continual reinforcement and prediction learning to human-machine partnerships such as intelligent prostheses and rehabilitation devices, as PI in the RLAI and BLINC labs.
question: How can continually learning agents form effective partnerships with people, for example in intelligent prosthetic limbs?

name: Pattern Recognition Lab (Andreas Maier)
summary: Applies deep and offline reinforcement learning to decision problems such as distribution-grid protection and trade execution.
question: How can deep RL be applied reliably to control and decision problems in energy systems and finance?

name: People and Robots Teaching and Learning (PoRTaL) (Sanjiban Choudhury)
primary: imitation and reinforcement learning for robots
summary: Works on imitation learning, reward learning and reinforcement learning so that robots and agents can learn skills from people.
question: How can robots learn everyday tasks from people in ways that are practical for everyday users?

name: People, AI, and Robotics (PAIR) Lab (Animesh Garg)
summary: Studies representations and algorithms for reinforcement learning and control that let robots acquire and transfer skills.
question: What structured inductive biases let robots acquire generalizable skills for interaction?

name: Perception, Action, & Learning Group (PennPAL) (Dinesh Jayaraman)
primary: robot learning with automated reward and environment design
summary: Works on robot learning, including frameworks in which foundation models write reward functions, simulation environments and controllers used to train robots with reinforcement learning.
question: How can robots be made easier to teach and more resource-efficient in the physical world?

name: Peter Vamplew group (Peter Vamplew)
institution: Federation University Australia (Institute of Innovation, Science and Sustainability)
summary: The group works on multi-objective reinforcement learning and its use for AI safety and explainability, including value-based MORL in stochastic environments and generalisation across environments.
question: How can reinforcement learning handle multiple conflicting objectives to make autonomous systems safer and more explainable?

name: Physical Intelligence (Karol Hausman; Sergey Levine; Chelsea Finn)
lead: Karol Hausman; Sergey Levine; Chelsea Finn
summary: Develops the pi-series robot foundation models and the Recap method for improving vision-language-action policies with RL from autonomous experience and human corrections.
question: How can a general-purpose robot foundation model keep improving from its own real-world experience?

name: Pierre-Luc Bacon group (Pierre-Luc Bacon)
summary: The group studies reinforcement learning and optimal control, particularly the curse of the horizon and representation learning, with applications to HVAC/energy, materials and drug discovery.
question: How can representation learning and ideas from optimal control help RL overcome the curse of the horizon?

name: Ping-Chun Hsieh group (Ping-Chun Hsieh)
institution: National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University (Department of Computer Science)
summary: The group studies bandit learning and reinforcement learning, including multi-objective, preference-based and action-constrained RL.
question: How can bandit and reinforcement learning algorithms be made efficient with limited or reward-free supervision?

name: Piotr Miłoś group (Piotr Miłoś)
summary: Studies off-policy and continual deep RL, including replay, overestimation and plasticity in actor-critic methods, and learned representations for planning.
question: Which methods can deliver robust decision-making in complex scenarios?

name: PKU Alignment and Interaction Research Lab (PAIR Lab) (Yaodong Yang)
summary: The lab works on constrained (safe) RL, multi-agent RL and game theory, and RL-based alignment and robot learning; it maintains open-source safe-RL tools such as Safety-Gymnasium, OmniSafe and Safe-RLHF.
question: How can constrained reinforcement learning and multi-agent game-theoretic modelling make learning agents reliably do what humans intend?

name: Prakash Panangaden group (Prakash Panangaden)
summary: The group studies probabilistic processes and their RL applications, including behavioural pseudometrics, representations in actor-critic methods and preference-based RL.
question: How can behavioural metrics on probabilistic processes inform representation and learning in RL?

name: Prashanth L.A. group (Prashanth L.A.)
institution: Indian Institute of Technology Madras (Department of CSE)
summary: The group develops risk-sensitive RL, bandit and stochastic optimization algorithms with convergence guarantees.
question: How can reinforcement learning and stochastic optimization account for risk with provable guarantees?

name: Prediction and Action Lab (PAL) (Josiah Hanna)
summary: Designs reinforcement learning algorithms and applies them to robots, including sim-to-real transfer and RoboCup soccer.
question: How can agents learn to make decisions on their own, improving through experience rather than fixed logic?

name: Princeton Reinforcement Learning Lab (Benjamin Eysenbach)
summary: Develops reinforcement learning algorithms, with a focus on self-supervised and goal-conditioned methods that propose their own goals and collect their own data.
question: How can reinforcement learning agents learn effectively by proposing their own goals and collecting their own data?

name: Prorok Lab (Amanda Prorok)
summary: Develops multi-agent RL and learning-based planning for multi-robot teams, including work on behavioural diversity and intention modelling.
question: How can collective intelligence be built for multi-robot systems?

name: Prosocial Dynamics Lab (Fernando P. Santos)
summary: Models populations of adaptive and RL agents to study cooperation and fairness, with applications to transport network design.
question: How do behavioral dynamics in systems of adaptive learning agents shape cooperation and fairness, and how can such systems be designed to be prosocial?

name: Proxima Intelligence Lab (Pi Lab) (Sung Whan Yoon)
summary: The lab studies machine intelligence and information theory, including robust reinforcement learning via flat reward landscapes and quantum speed-ups for robust RL.
question: Why are some reinforcement-learning policies robust to perturbation, and how can that robustness be obtained efficiently?

name: Psychology of Information Processing Lab (Constantin Rothkopf)
summary: The lab models human perception, decision-making and action with inverse reinforcement learning and Bayesian methods and compares deep RL agents with human behaviour.
question: How do humans use perception actively during extended natural behaviour to form beliefs and guide goal-directed decisions and actions?

name: Qiaomin Xie group
summary: Develops theory and algorithms for reinforcement learning, including offline actor-critic methods for average-reward MDPs and stable offline value-function learning.
question: How can reinforcement learning algorithms be made provably stable and sample-efficient in stochastic systems?

name: Quantum Computing group, Fraunhofer IKS (Jeanette Miriam Lorenz)
summary: Benchmarks and implements quantum reinforcement learning algorithms, including single-file reference implementations.
question: How can quantum reinforcement learning be benchmarked fairly against classical methods?

name: Quantum Information & Computation Group (Hans J. Briegel)
summary: Develops projective simulation, a physics-inspired model of learning agents, and uses RL agents to study agency and emergent collective behaviour.
question: How can physical models of learning explain and implement agency in artificial agents?

name: Qwen Team RL (Alibaba)
summary: Develops RL algorithms for training Qwen language models, including Group Sequence Policy Optimization (GSPO) and Soft Adaptive Policy Optimization (SAPO).
question: How can RL training of large (including mixture-of-experts) language models be made stable and efficient?

name: R. Srikant group
summary: Analyses the convergence and scalability of reinforcement learning algorithms, including policy-gradient methods for average-reward MDPs and POMDPs.
question: What convergence and sample-complexity guarantees can be proved for reinforcement learning algorithms?

name: Rafał Kucharski lab (Rafał Kucharski)
summary: Uses multi-agent reinforcement learning to study how autonomous vehicles' collective behaviour affects urban traffic, and how agents cooperate with changing partners.
question: How will autonomous vehicles trained with reinforcement learning change urban traffic dynamics?

name: Rahul Jain group
institution: University of Southern California; Google DeepMind
summary: Studies stochastic control, online RL and preference-based optimization for aligning generative models.
question: How should learning agents control stochastic systems and align with human preferences efficiently?

name: RAI Institute (Marc Raibert)
summary: Develops RL controllers for dynamic robots such as Spot and the Ultra Mobility Vehicle, including acrobatic bicycle manoeuvres learned with RL.
question: How can learning-based control give robots athletic, dynamic mobility in the real world?

name: Raman Arora group (Raman Arora)
summary: The group develops learning theory for reinforcement learning and Markov games, including policy regret and unlearning in RL.
question: What guarantees can learning agents achieve against adaptive opponents in sequential games?

name: Ramponi Group (Giorgia Ramponi)
summary: Studies the theory and algorithms of inverse RL, imitation and preference-based RL, and multi-agent learning.
question: How can agents learn objectives and policies from demonstrations and preferences, alone and in multi-agent settings?

name: Real Life Reinforcement Learning Lab – RL3 (Marcello Restelli)
summary: The group develops reinforcement-learning algorithms with theoretical guarantees, including policy-gradient, imitation and inverse RL methods, and applies them to domains such as energy, finance and robotics.
question: How can reinforcement-learning algorithms be designed for complex environments while keeping both theoretical guarantees and real-world applicability?

name: Reasoning and Learning Research Group (Yang Gao)
institution: Nanjing University (School of Intelligence Science and Technology)
summary: The group studies multi-agent and single-agent reinforcement learning, including communication-constrained and decentralized cooperative MARL and causal structure learning for model-based RL.
question: How can multiple learning agents cooperate efficiently under limited communication and partial information?

name: Reinforced Decision Intelligence Lab (Donghwan Lee)
summary: The lab develops reinforcement learning and learning-based control with mathematical guarantees, using control-theoretic tools such as switching-system analysis of Q-learning.
question: How can learning systems make effective decisions while remaining stable, robust, and safe?

name: Reinforcement Learning and Artificial Intelligence Lab, RLAI (Richard S. Sutton)
primary: continual RL and the Alberta Plan
summary: Sutton works on the simple general principles of learning from experience (temporal-difference learning, continual learning, average-reward RL, the Alberta Plan and OaK architecture) as a quarter-time professor at the University of Alberta, with most of his current research done at the startup Oak Lab.
question: What simple general principles underlie both natural and artificial intelligence, and how can an agent learn them from its own experience?

name: Reinforcement Learning and Computational Decision-Making (Carlo D'Eramo)
summary: Develops methods that make deep RL more efficient and practical, including stable value estimation, multi-agent policy gradients, and transfer, curriculum and multi-task learning.
question: How can reinforcement learning be made efficient and practical enough for challenging real-world decision-making and control?

name: Reinforcement Learning Group Dresden (Ostap Okhrin)
summary: The group applies deep reinforcement learning to autonomous driving and vessels, including safe RL for rare-event risk control in urban driving.
question: How can reinforcement learning make autonomous vehicles and vessels in transport safer and more efficient?

name: Reinforcement Learning Group Leiden (Thomas Moerland; Aske Plaat)
summary: Researches the combination of planning and learning in RL, plus safe RL, zero-shot RL and RL for language-model agents.
question: How can planning and learning be combined so that agents learn through trial and error more effectively?

name: Reinforcement Learning Research Labs (Shie Mannor)
institution: Technion – Israel Institute of Technology; NVIDIA Research
summary: The group develops theory and algorithms for sequential decision making, including robust MDPs, policy-gradient methods, world-model agents and RL with large or combinatorial action spaces.
question: How should agents act and make decisions in dynamic, complex and uncertain environments?

name: Reliable Autonomous Systems Lab (REALM) (Chuchu Fan)
primary: safe RL and certified learning for control
summary: Develops certified learning-based control, including safe multi-agent RL with control barrier functions, RL for reach-avoid problems and offline RL.
question: How can learning-enabled autonomous systems be made certifiably safe?

name: Rhine AI Lab (Ilija Bogunovic)
primary: RL for LLMs and robust decision making
summary: Develops RL and bandit methods for language-model post-training, regret-driven world-model learning and robust sequential decision making.
question: How can learning agents make sample-efficient and robust sequential decisions, from bandits to RL post-training of language models?

name: Risk Analytics and Optimization Chair (Daniel Kuhn)
summary: Develops distributionally robust optimization methods for dynamic decision problems, including robust Markov decision processes and bandits.
question: How can large-scale dynamic decision problems under uncertainty be modelled and solved reliably?

name: Robert Loftin (University of Sheffield)
summary: Applies multi-agent RL to ad hoc collaboration between AI agents and humans.
question: How can AI agents learn to cooperate with new partners, including humans, without prior coordination?

name: Robot Learning Lab (Abhinav Valada)
summary: The lab works on robot learning for mobility and manipulation, including RL fine-tuning of diffusion policies inside learned world models and self-play driving policies.
question: How can robot learning algorithms for mobility and manipulation reach autonomy at scale?

name: Robot Learning Lab (Aviv Tamar)
summary: The lab works on reinforcement learning and its connections to representation learning and planning, with applications to robot manipulation and tactile sensing.
question: How can machines learn models of their environments that are useful for tasks, and learn behaviour from interaction in an interpretable and safe manner?

name: Robot Learning Lab (Edward Johns)
summary: Develops imitation and RL methods for robot manipulation, including large-scale simulated RL from generated object models.
question: How can robots learn manipulation skills efficiently and generally enough to assist in everyday environments?

name: Robot Learning Laboratory (RLLAB) (Songhwai Oh)
institution: Seoul National University (Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering)
primary: safe and offline RL for robots
summary: The lab studies robot learning, including safe RL, offline goal-conditioned RL and multi-agent learning for manipulation and navigation.
question: How can robots learn safe and reliable behaviour from data and interaction?

name: Robot Learning Laboratory, NAIST (Takamitsu Matsubara)
institution: Nara Institute of Science and Technology (NAIST)
summary: The lab applies machine learning, including RL and imitation learning, to real robots such as manipulators and excavators.
question: How can machine learning give robots advanced intelligence for real-world tasks?

name: Robot Learning Team, RIKEN AIP (Takayuki Osa)
institution: RIKEN Center for Advanced Intelligence Project
summary: The team develops deep reinforcement learning algorithms, including offline and ensemble policy optimisation and cross-embodiment offline RL for robots.
question: How can robots learn stable and efficient policies from diverse data and interaction?

name: Robot Perception and Learning Lab (RPL) (Yuke Zhu)
institution: University of Texas at Austin; NVIDIA
summary: Develops perception and learning methods, including imitation and reinforcement learning, for general-purpose robot autonomy.
question: How can closing the perception-action loop give rise to general-purpose robot autonomy?

name: Robot Perception and Learning Lab – RPL (Dimitrios Kanoulas)
summary: Develops RL pipelines for legged locomotion and loco-manipulation, including VLM-based automated reward design and sim-to-real deployment.
question: How can articulated robots perceive, decide and control themselves to operate autonomously in unpredictable natural environments?

name: Robot Vision & Learning Lab, RVL (Florian Shkurti)
summary: The lab works on robot learning, including offline-to-online actor-critic transfer, imitation learning and evaluation of robot policies.
question: How can robots learn robust control policies from data and interaction?

name: Robotic AI & Learning Lab (Sergey Levine)
primary: deep RL for robotics and LLMs
summary: Develops deep RL algorithms (offline, goal-conditioned, value-based) and applies them to robot control and language-model agents.
question: How can machines acquire flexible, adaptable behavior autonomously through learning?

name: Robotic Systems Lab (Marco Hutter)
summary: Trains locomotion and manipulation controllers for legged robots and construction machines with simulation-based deep RL and learned world models, deployed on hardware.
question: How can new control and learning algorithms give legged robots dynamic, versatile locomotion and manipulation in the real world?

name: Robotics and Artificial Intelligence Lab (RaiLab) (Jemin Hwangbo)
summary: The lab uses reinforcement learning and simulation to train locomotion and motor skills for legged robots and legged manipulators it designs.
question: How can robots autonomously acquire agile locomotion and complex motor skills through reinforcement learning?

name: Robotics and Embodied AI Lab, REAL (Glen Berseth; Liam Paull)
summary: The lab works on sequential decision making for robots and other embodied agents, including RL for generalist robots, safe exploration and benchmarks for RL agents.
question: How can we build generalist robots and embodied agents that learn to make sequential decisions in the real world?

name: Robotics and Intelligent Systems group – ROBIN (Jim Tørresen)
summary: Tørresen's group works on bio-inspired and adaptive robotics, including deep reinforcement learning for multi-robot navigation and LLM-assisted decision making.
question: How can bio-inspired computing and machine learning make robots adapt in complex real-world settings?

name: Robotics and Perception Group (Davide Scaramuzza)
summary: Trains quadrotor controllers with model-free, model-based and multi-agent RL for agile vision-based flight and drone racing, transferred from simulation to real drones.
question: How can autonomous drones navigate using only onboard cameras and computation, without external infrastructure?

name: Robotics, Autonomous Intelligence and Learning Lab – RAIL (Benjamin Rosman; Steven James)
summary: The lab works on reinforcement learning and robotics, including hierarchical skill discovery, reward-machine RL, safe offline RL and compositional transfer.
question: How can a single generally intelligent agent become competent across many tasks by learning and composing reusable skills?

name: Robotics, Perception and Learning Lab (Danica Kragic)
summary: The lab works on robot manipulation and learning, including preference-based and safe reinforcement learning and visuomotor diffusion policies.
question: How can robots combine perception and machine learning to act and manipulate in the physical world?

name: Robots Perceiving and Doing Lab (David Held)
summary: The lab develops perception and learning methods, including reinforcement learning and policy adaptation, for robot manipulation of deformable and articulated objects.
question: How can robots perceive and act in cluttered everyday environments?

name: Robust Autonomy and Decisions Group – RAD (Subramanian Ramamoorthy)
primary: robust robot learning and world models
summary: Studies learning and adaptation for robots under uncertainty, including world models that RL agents exploit and how to repair them.
question: How can autonomous robots learn and adapt to cope with the uncertain and the unknown?

name: Robust Decision-making & Learning Lab (Hanna Kurniawati)
summary: The lab develops scalable solvers for sequential decision making under uncertainty (POMDPs), integrated planning and learning, and reinforcement learning for robots.
question: How can robots operate reliably, resiliently and safely by making principled sequential decisions under uncertainty?

name: Ronald Parr group (Ronald Parr)
summary: The group studies value function approximation and off-policy reinforcement learning, including linear methods and policy sampling.
question: How can value-function approximation be made stable and accurate for off-policy reinforcement learning?

name: Ruosong Wang group (Ruosong Wang)
institution: Peking University (Center on Frontiers of Computing Studies)
summary: The group studies the theoretical foundations of reinforcement learning, designing provably efficient algorithms and proving sample-complexity lower bounds under function approximation.
question: What are the fundamental statistical and computational limits of reinforcement learning, and which algorithms reach them?

name: Rupam Mahmood group (A. Rupam Mahmood)
primary: continual and streaming RL for robots
summary: The group develops continual reinforcement and representation learning algorithms and real-time learning systems, including streaming deep RL and RL that runs onboard physical robots.
question: What scalable and general learning mechanisms let agents keep improving continually, including when controlling physical robots in real time?

name: Rutgers Robot Learning Lab (Abdeslam Boularias)
summary: Develops reinforcement learning methods for robot manipulation, including residual RL on high of vision-language-action policies and sim-to-real insertion.
question: How can a robot learn from its own experience to perform complex manipulation tasks?

name: Rycolab (Ryan Cotterell)
summary: NLP lab whose RL work covers RL post-training with search-informed process rewards and KL-divergence estimation for RLHF.
question: How can formal and statistical methods improve the training and reasoning of language models?

name: Sabatelli group (Matthia Sabatelli)
summary: Studies the learning dynamics of deep RL agents, including plasticity loss, double descent and low-dimensional representations.
question: What happens inside deep RL networks during training, and how can that knowledge make agents learn more reliably?

name: Safe AI Lab (Ding Zhao)
summary: Develops learning methods for trustworthy physical AI agents, including safe and multi-agent reinforcement learning for humanoids, robots and autonomous vehicles.
question: How can generalist AI agents be made trustworthy for safety-critical physical applications?

name: Safe Autonomous Systems Lab (Sylvia Herbert)
summary: Combines Hamilton-Jacobi reachability and optimal control with learning to obtain safety assurances, including RL with reach-avoid objectives.
question: How can autonomous systems obtain scalable safety assurances that adapt quickly to new information?

name: Safe Whole-body Intelligent Robotics Lab – SWIRL (Stephen James)
summary: Works at the intersection of online RL, offline RL and imitation learning for robots, including humanoid manipulation benchmarks.
question: How can robots learn safely and sample-efficiently using their entire physical embodiment?

name: Safe, Confident, and Aligned Learning + Robotics Lab (SCALAR) (Scott Niekum)
summary: Develops learning algorithms that enforce safety constraints, provide performance guarantees and align agent objectives with human objectives, using imitation and reinforcement learning.
question: How can AI systems be aligned with human objectives and deployed safely in the real world?

name: Sarah Dean group
summary: Studies the fundamentals of data-driven control and sequential decision-making, including policy gradient methods and policies for systems with feedback and participation dynamics.
question: How do optimization, machine learning and dynamics interact in data-driven methods for control and decision-making?

name: Satinder Singh group
summary: Works on reinforcement learning agents that learn in complex, dynamic environments, including questions of agency, world models and game playing.
question: How can autonomous agents learn to act well in complex, dynamic environments?

name: Saxe Lab (Andrew Saxe)
institution: University College London (Gatsby Computational Neuroscience Unit)
summary: Develops mathematical theory of learning in deep networks and brains, including an analysis of how RL post-training builds compositional reasoning strategies.
question: What mathematical principles describe how learning unfolds in brains and deep neural networks?

name: Scalable Robot Learning Lab (Youngwoon Lee)
institution: Seoul National University (Department of Computer Science and Engineering)
summary: The lab develops scalable reinforcement learning methods, such as model-based offline RL with action chunks, for humanoid control and dexterous robot manipulation.
question: How can scalable reinforcement learning help robots learn complex real-world tasks?

name: Schultz Lab (Wolfram Schultz)
summary: Records reward and decision signals in primate dopamine and amygdala neurons and relates them to learning-theory and economic constructs.
question: Which brain signals implement the theoretical constructs underlying reward-seeking, learning and economic choice?

name: SCOPE Lab (Abhishek Dubey)
summary: The lab develops sequential decision-making methods, including planning and RL in non-stationary environments, for transit and emergency-response systems.
question: How can decision procedures adapt online when the environment keeps changing?

name: Sebastian Risi group (Sebastian Risi)
summary: Risi's group studies neuroevolution, self-organising and open-ended systems, including evolutionary approaches to continual reinforcement learning.
question: Can we create lifelong learning machines that continuously acquire new knowledge and skills?

name: Self-Organizing Systems Lab (Heinz Koeppl)
summary: The lab studies large ensembles of interacting agents and uses mean-field reinforcement learning and control for large-scale multi-agent problems.
question: How can large ensembles of reconfigurable agents collectively solve complex tasks such as self-assembly, distributed sensing and control?

name: Sequential Decision Making group – Spaan lab (Matthijs Spaan)
summary: Studies uncertainty-aware and Bayesian deep RL, safe exploration and search-based planning for agents acting under partial observability.
question: How can agents plan and learn good policies over time when their models of the world are uncertain?

name: Sequential Intelligence Lab (Shangtong Zhang)
