summary: Studies theoretical and empirical aspects of reinforcement learning, including convergence of TD learning and Q-learning and in-context RL.
question: When do reinforcement learning algorithms provably converge, and why?

name: Serena Booth group (Serena Booth)
summary: The group studies how people specify, inspect and revise objectives for RL agents and robots, including reward alignment metrics.
question: How can people specify, inspect and revise the behaviour of AI and robot learners?

name: Seung-Woo Seo group (Seung-Woo Seo)
institution: Seoul National University (Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering)
summary: The group studies reinforcement learning for intelligent vehicles and robots, including hierarchical policies for long-horizon offline goal-conditioned RL and unsupervised skill discovery.
question: How can autonomous agents learn long-horizon behaviour in complex, non-stationary environments?

name: Sham Kakade group
summary: Works on mathematical foundations of learning systems, including policy optimization and reinforcement learning, and on training pipelines for foundation models and interactive agents.
question: What principles govern large-scale learning systems and agents that learn from interaction?

name: Shao-Hua Sun group (Shao-Hua Sun)
institution: National Taiwan University (Department of Electrical Engineering)
primary: RL, robot learning and program synthesis
summary: The group works on robot learning, reinforcement learning and program synthesis, including programmatic RL policies and learning from suboptimal demonstrations.
question: How can agents learn interpretable and generalizable policies by combining reinforcement learning with program synthesis?

name: Sheila McIlraith group (Sheila A. McIlraith)
primary: reward machines and formal methods in RL
summary: The group combines knowledge representation, formal languages and planning with reinforcement learning, including reward machines and grounding language in agent behaviour.
question: How can formal languages and symbolic knowledge, such as reward machines, make reinforcement learning agents more sample-efficient and aligned?

name: Shibhansh Dohare (Keen Technologies)
city: Dallas (company HQ; personal location not stated)
summary: Studies loss of plasticity in deep continual learning and RL and methods such as continual backpropagation and selective weight reinitialization to maintain it.
question: How can neural networks keep learning new things indefinitely without losing plasticity?

name: Shipra Agrawal group
summary: Develops algorithms and theory for multi-armed bandits, online learning and reinforcement learning, with applications in operations research.
question: How should agents learn to make sequential decisions under uncertainty with provable guarantees?

name: Shivaram Kalyanakrishnan group (Shivaram Kalyanakrishnan)
institution: Indian Institute of Technology Bombay (Department of CSE)
summary: The group studies sequential decision-making, including MDP planning, policy iteration, multi-armed bandits and multiagent learning.
question: How can agents, especially ones that learn, make good sequential decisions efficiently?

name: Shuai Li group (Shuai Li)
institution: Shanghai Jiao Tong University (John Hopcroft Center for Computer Science)
summary: The group designs reinforcement learning and multi-armed bandit algorithms with regret analysis, including offline-to-online RL, adversarial MDPs and learning in matching markets and games.
question: How can reinforcement learning and bandit algorithms be designed with provable regret guarantees?

name: Shuang Qiu group (Shuang Qiu)
institution: City University of Hong Kong (Department of Data Science)
summary: The group studies reinforcement learning theory and algorithms, including robust cross-domain and model-based offline RL, and RL-based credit assignment for language-model agents.
question: How can agents learn reliable policies from offline data collected under shifted dynamics?

name: Siamak Ravanbakhsh group (Siamak Ravanbakhsh)
summary: The group studies probabilistic reasoning, generative modelling and sequential decision making, with RL work on model-based offline RL, sampling-based exploration and symmetry.
question: How can symmetry and generative modelling improve probabilistic reasoning and sequential decision making?

name: Sicun Gao group (Sicun Gao)
summary: The group studies policy optimisation and value estimation in on-policy reinforcement learning and links RL with control and automated reasoning.
question: What makes policy-gradient reinforcement learning succeed or fail on hard control problems?

name: Simon S. Du group
summary: Proves sample-complexity and regret guarantees for RL and studies RL for language-model reasoning and human-AI coordination.
question: What are the fundamental statistical and computational limits of reinforcement learning?

name: Siqi Shen group (Siqi Shen)
summary: The group studies multi-agent reinforcement learning, including value factorisation, parameter sharing and diffusion-based offline MARL, alongside embodied AI and agents.
question: How can multiple agents learn to cooperate efficiently and robustly with reinforcement learning?

name: Siva Theja Maguluri group
summary: Studies finite-sample convergence of the stochastic approximation algorithms that underlie reinforcement learning, such as TD learning and Q-learning.
question: What finite-sample guarantees hold for reinforcement learning algorithms viewed as stochastic approximation?

name: Skild AI (Deepak Pathak; Abhinav Gupta)
summary: Builds the Skild Brain robot foundation model and post-trains it with reinforcement learning and physical self-play in simulation.
question: Can a single robot brain learn general physical skills across embodiments, improving through reinforcement learning and self-play?

name: SLURM Lab (Daniel Seita)
summary: Develops learning methods, including reward learning and sim-to-real policy learning, for manipulating geometrically and perceptually challenging objects.
question: How can robots reliably manipulate challenging objects in less-structured real-world settings?

name: SMART Lab (Byung-Cheol Min)
summary: The lab develops robot learning for multi-robot and human-robot teams, including preference-based reinforcement learning and reward learning.
question: How can multiple robots learn to collaborate with each other and with humans?

name: Smart Sensing and Robotics (SSR) Lab (Wenbo Ding)
summary: Alongside robotic tactile sensing, the lab develops reinforcement learning methods, including off-policy RL for flow-based policies and policy-gradient/Newton methods in kernel spaces.
question: How can robots sense and learn to act efficiently in contact-rich interaction with the physical world?

name: Social RL Lab (Natasha Jaques)
summary: Studies RL algorithms that use social information in multi-agent and human-AI interaction, including self-play and RL fine-tuning of LLMs.
question: Can social reinforcement learning help AI agents learn complex behaviour, adapt and cooperate the way social learning helps humans?

name: Soft Robotics Lab (Robert Katzschmann)
primary: rl for dexterous and soft robots
summary: Applies offline and real-world RL to dexterous robot hands and to bio-inspired soft and underwater robots.
question: How can robots built from soft, rigid and living materials learn adaptive interactions with their environments?

name: Songbird Group, Institute of Neuroinformatics (Richard Hahnloser)
institution: University of Zurich and ETH Zurich
summary: Studies how zebra finches learn song and analyses their learning strategies and motor exploration with RL theory.
question: Which reinforcement-learning strategies do songbirds use to learn their songs, and how does the avian brain implement them?

name: Sony AI Gran Turismo Sophy team (Peter Wurman; Peter Stone)
summary: Develops GT Sophy, a deep RL racing agent for Gran Turismo, and extends it to vision-based control and automated reward design with foundation models.
question: How can reinforcement learning agents reach champion-level performance in complex real-time games while behaving as specified?

name: Sony AI – Zurich (Peter Dürr)
summary: Builds real-time robot systems trained with model-free RL, including a table-tennis robot competitive with elite players, and links RL to optimal control.
question: How can RL control physical robots in fast, adversarial real-time interaction such as table tennis?

name: Space Robotics group – SpaceR (Miguel Olivares-Mendez)
summary: Trains RL controllers and benchmarks for spacecraft docking, inspection, planetary robots and fault-tolerant control.
question: How can robots learn to operate autonomously in space and planetary environments?

name: Spatial AI group (Matthias Schubert)
primary: RL for mobility and resource allocation
summary: Applies reinforcement learning, including offline RL with diffusion world models, to mobility and resource-allocation tasks.
question: How can RL agents be trained to optimize mobility and resource-allocation decisions?

name: Sriram Ganapathi Subramanian group (Sriram Ganapathi Subramanian)
summary: The group works on multi-agent reinforcement learning at the intersection with game theory, addressing scale, non-stationarity, communication and safety.
question: How can multi-agent learning systems overcome scale, non-stationarity, communication and sample-inefficiency problems?

name: STAIR Lab (Hao Su)
institution: Fudan University (Institute of General Physical Intelligence)
summary: The lab works on embodied AI and robot learning, including GPU-parallel simulation (ManiSkill), massively parallel on-policy RL and world models for control.
question: How can simulation, large-scale reinforcement learning and world models give robots a real understanding of the physical world?

name: Stanford Intelligent Systems Laboratory (Mykel Kochenderfer)
summary: Develops algorithms for robust sequential decision making under uncertainty, with applications to air traffic control and unmanned aircraft.
question: How can optimal decision strategies be derived efficiently from high-dimensional probabilistic problem representations while maintaining safety?

name: Statistical Reinforcement Learning Lab (Susan Murphy)
summary: Develops reinforcement learning and statistical methods for personalizing sequential treatments, including just-in-time adaptive interventions delivered by mobile devices.
question: How can online reinforcement learning safely personalize health interventions delivered in daily life?

name: Stochastic Systems Laboratory (Shalabh Bhatnagar)
institution: Indian Institute of Science (Department of Computer Science and Automation)
summary: The lab develops and analyses stochastic approximation algorithms for control and optimization, especially reinforcement learning and actor-critic methods.
question: How can stochastic approximation algorithms for reinforcement learning and simulation optimization be designed with provable convergence?

name: Supaero Reinforcement Learning Initiative – SuReLI (Emmanuel Rachelson)
summary: Studies RL and sequential decision problems, including model-based RL for exact combinatorial optimization.
question: How do learning and optimization mechanisms work in sequential decision problems, and how can they be improved?

name: Swiss AI Lab IDSIA – Schmidhuber Group (Jürgen Schmidhuber)
summary: Works on upside-down RL, curiosity-driven agents, world models and policy optimization, with group members affiliated with IDSIA and KAUST.
question: How can an AI system improve itself through curiosity-driven exploration, world models and learning to learn?

name: SYCAMORE – Systems Control and Multiagent Optimization Research (Maryam Kamgarpour)
summary: Develops theory for multi-agent RL, inverse RL and constrained or safe RL, building on game theory and stochastic control.
question: How can multiple agents make good decisions in uncertain and dynamic environments?

name: Sylvain Lamprier (robust and offline RL)
summary: Works on robust, offline and exploration-driven deep RL, including style-aligned offline RL and reward-preserving attacks.
question: How can deep RL agents learn diverse, robust behaviors from limited or adversarial data?

name: Systems Intelligence Lab (Jinkyoo Park)
institution: KAIST (Department of Industrial and Systems Engineering)
summary: The lab develops reinforcement learning and multi-agent RL methods for combinatorial optimisation and control of complex systems, such as RL4CO, with applications in logistics, manufacturing and molecular design.
question: How can data-driven and reinforcement-learning methods optimise the design and operation of complex engineering systems?

name: Sébastien Gros (NTNU Engineering Cybernetics)
institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)
summary: Gros's group combines reinforcement learning with model predictive control to obtain safe, data-driven controllers for energy, process and vehicle systems.
question: How can reinforcement learning and model predictive control be combined into safe, data-driven controllers?

name: Tactile Robotics (Nathan Lepora)
summary: Trains deep RL policies with tactile feedback for dexterous manipulation and sim-to-real transfer.
question: How can robots achieve dexterous manipulation through artificial touch?

name: TEA Lab (Simon Stepputtis)
summary: The lab works on robot learning and multi-agent coordination, including policy-gradient and diffusion-policy methods.
question: How can robots and agents learn policies that coordinate with novel partners?

name: Teamcore (Milind Tambe)
summary: Teamcore applies multi-agent systems and reinforcement learning, including restless bandits and combinatorial-action RL, to resource allocation in public health and conservation.
question: How can AI and reinforcement learning allocate scarce resources to improve outcomes for underserved communities?

name: Technical Aspects of Multimodal Systems – TAMS (Jianwei Zhang)
summary: The group develops robot learning methods, including curriculum reinforcement learning for agile skills and RL-based whole-body control for humanoids.
question: How can multimodal robots learn agile and compositional skills, such as humanoid loco-manipulation, from interaction?

name: Tengyang Xie group (Tengyang Xie)
summary: The group studies the theory and algorithms of reinforcement learning, including offline RL, exploration and outcome-based RL for language-model reasoning.
question: What makes reinforcement learning sample-efficient when feedback arrives only as outcomes or preferences?

name: Thanh H. Nguyen group (Thanh Nguyen)
summary: The group develops offline cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning, multi-agent imitation and preference learning, and game-theoretic security models.
question: How can teams of agents learn coordinated policies from fixed or mixed-quality data?

name: The Movement Lab (C. Karen Liu)
primary: RL for physics-based characters and humanoids
summary: Develops physics-based control for simulated characters and humanoid robots, including RL motion-tracking controllers, flow-policy gradient methods and real-world policy adaptation.
question: How can simulated characters and humanoid robots learn agile, physically grounded movement and interaction skills?

name: Theoretical and Cognitive Neuroscience lab (Rubén Moreno-Bote)
summary: The lab combines computational and cognitive neuroscience to study how brains decide and learn from reward, and contributes to reinforcement-learning methods such as successor features.
question: What computational principles let brains perceive, decide and learn from reward, and how can they inform learning agents?

name: Theory of Machine Learning / Optimization of Adaptive Systems (Tobias Glasmachers)
primary: structured deep rl and industrial rl
summary: The group adds structure to deep reinforcement learning for navigation and industrial control and combines RL with evolutionary optimisation.
question: How can deep reinforcement learning systems be given additional structure to become truly autonomous, e.g. for efficient navigation and object-oriented actions?

name: Thiago D. Simão (safe RL)
summary: Develops safe RL algorithms and GPU-accelerated benchmarks for settings with constrained interaction with an unknown environment.
question: How can agents learn good behavior in unknown environments while respecting safety constraints during learning?

name: Ti-Rong Wu group (Ti-Rong Wu)
summary: The group studies reinforcement learning and planning for games, including AlphaZero/MuZero variants (MiniZero, OptionZero), search control, game solving and human-like RL agents.
question: How can reinforcement learning and search be combined to master and solve complex games efficiently?

name: Tian Lan group (Tian Lan)
institution: The George Washington University (Department of ECE)
summary: The group develops multi-agent reinforcement learning and multi-agent Monte Carlo tree search methods and studies the structure of value functions.
question: How can many agents plan and learn coordinated policies efficiently in large joint action spaces?

name: Tien Mai group (Tien Mai)
institution: Singapore Management University (School of Computing and Information Systems)
summary: The group works on inverse reinforcement learning and offline imitation and multi-agent RL, using distribution-correction (DICE) methods and links to discrete choice models.
question: How can agents learn good behaviour from offline demonstrations of mixed quality?

name: Tong Zhang group (Tong Zhang)
summary: The group analyses KL-regularised reinforcement learning, contextual bandits and RLHF, and develops RL training methods for reasoning in large language models.
question: What are the statistical limits and efficient algorithms for reinforcement learning from human and verifiable feedback?

name: Toronto Intelligent Systems Lab, TISL (Igor Gilitschenski)
summary: The lab works on embodied AI and robot learning, including goal-conditioned and value-aware model-based RL and reward-hacking detection.
question: How can embodied agents learn efficiently in simulation and the real world, inspired by human learning?

name: Tresp Lab (Volker Tresp)
summary: Develops reinforcement learning methods for language-model agents, such as RL-trained memory management and efficient rollout reuse.
question: How can reinforcement learning give language-model agents better memory, reasoning and tool use?

name: Triesch Lab (Jochen Triesch)
summary: The lab models brain development and builds developmental AI agents that learn autonomously, using intrinsic rewards and deep reinforcement learning.
question: How can artificial agents learn completely autonomously, like infants and children, by exploring and interacting with the world?

name: Trusted AI Group (Bettina Könighofer)
summary: Combines formal verification, reactive synthesis and machine learning to build shields and runtime enforcement that keep reinforcement learning agents safe.
question: How can formal methods provide safety guarantees for learning-enabled autonomous systems?

name: trustml@Penn (Osbert Bastani)
primary: trustworthy RL and RL for LLMs
summary: Works on trustworthy machine learning, including reinforcement learning for language-model reasoning and inference-aware policy optimization.
question: How can learned decision-making policies be made reliable and trustworthy?

name: Trustworthy Cyber-Physical Systems group (Ezio Bartocci)
summary: Studies the specification, verification and interpretation of RL policies, including rule-based explanations of continuous-action policies.
question: How can RL policies used in cyber-physical systems be specified, verified and explained?

name: Tsinghua Embodied AI Lab (TEA Lab) (Huazhe Xu)
institution: Tsinghua University (IIIS); Shanghai Qi Zhi Institute
summary: The lab builds robot hardware and learning methods, including visual reinforcement learning and RL-based steering of pretrained robot policies, for real-world manipulation.
question: How can robots be built and then given the intelligence to learn manipulation skills efficiently in the real world?

name: Uchida Lab (Naoshige Uchida; Mitsuko Watabe-Uchida)
summary: The lab records and manipulates dopamine and striatal circuits in rodents to test reinforcement-learning accounts of reward learning, including distributional and temporal-difference learning.
question: What are the neural mechanisms for learning based on rewards and punishments?

name: UCLA AGI Lab (Quanquan Gu)
summary: Studies theory and algorithms for bandits, offline policy learning and RL from human feedback for language models.
question: What are the foundations of reinforcement learning and generative AI, and how can they accelerate discovery?

name: UW Robot Learning Laboratory (Byron Boots)
summary: Combines model predictive control, world models and inverse RL for robot learning, including off-road navigation and imitation from observation.
question: How can robots learn to act from observation and online world models in the real world?

name: Vaneet Aggarwal group
summary: Studies algorithms and guarantees for reinforcement learning, including constrained, average-reward and robust Markov decision processes.
question: What convergence and regret guarantees are achievable for constrained and average-reward reinforcement learning with general policies?

name: Verguts lab – computational cognitive neuroscience (Tom Verguts)
summary: Builds computational models of how humans adapt learning rates, explore and control behavior in changing environments.
question: How do humans adapt their learning and control strategies to the structure of their environment?

name: Vernade Lab (Claire Vernade)
summary: Studies the theory of sequential decision-making, including bandit algorithms with complex or delayed feedback and lifelong and meta-reinforcement learning.
question: What principles allow interactive learning systems to adapt reliably as their tasks and feedback change?

name: Vesoma (Martin Riedmiller)
summary: Humanoid-robot start-up registered in December 2025 whose AI research, led by Martin Riedmiller, aims at robots that learn tasks through their own real-world interaction.
question: How can humanoid robots become self-improving agents that learn new tasks from their own interaction with the world?

name: Vincent François-Lavet group (Vincent François-Lavet)
summary: Studies deep RL agents that generalize from limited data, with a focus on representation learning, world models and applications such as energy trading.
question: How can agents learn sequential decision-making tasks while generalizing from limited data?

name: Vision and Autonomy Intelligence Lab (Bolei Zhou)
primary: RL for driving and urban agents
summary: Builds simulators (e.g. MetaDrive, UrbanVerse) and RL/human-in-the-loop learning methods for autonomous driving and urban navigation.
question: How can efficient, generalizable physical AI be built that aligns with humans in complex urban environments?

name: Visual Intelligence for Transportation – VITA (Alexandre Alahi)
summary: Applies RL and world models to safe social navigation and autonomous mobility, and RL to the training of LLM meta-agents.
question: How can machines interpret and anticipate human behaviour to move safely and efficiently among people?

name: Walton Lab (Mark Walton)
summary: Studies how dopamine and frontal-striatal circuits encode reward, effort and prediction errors during value learning in rodents.
question: How are different aspects of value learned and used to guide decisions, and how does dopamine regulate this moment by moment?

name: Wei Pan (Newcastle University)
summary: Develops RL and learning-based control methods for robots with stability and safety guarantees.
question: How can Bayesian machine learning and the principles of dynamic control be combined to control robots and multi-robot systems?

name: WEIRD Lab (Abhishek Gupta)
summary: Develops RL algorithms and systems for real-world robotic manipulation, including large-scale RL and fine-tuning of generative control policies.
question: How can robots learn reliable manipulation in the home through real-world reinforcement learning?

name: Weitong Zhang group (Weitong Zhang)
institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (School of Data and Information Sciences)
summary: The group studies reinforcement learning algorithms with theoretical grounding, including Q-learning variants, offline RL and in-context policy optimisation.
question: How can value-based and offline reinforcement learning be made both provable and practical?

name: Wen Sun group (Wen Sun)
summary: The group develops provably efficient reinforcement learning, imitation learning and RL-from-human-feedback algorithms and applies them to post-training of large language models.
question: How can reinforcement and imitation learning be made both provably sample-efficient and practical at scale?

name: Witten Lab (Ilana Witten)
summary: The lab studies how learning and credit-assignment algorithms map onto brain circuitry, including dopamine value signals and learning from delayed outcomes.
question: How do learning and decision-making algorithms for credit assignment in complex, high-dimensional environments map onto brain circuitry?

name: Wouter van Heeswijk (RL for operations)
summary: Applies RL to operations research and finance problems, including large discrete and hybrid action spaces.
question: How can RL handle the large, structured action spaces of real operations and financial decision problems?

name: Xiangfeng Wang group (Xiangfeng Wang)
institution: East China Normal University (School of Computer Science and Technology)
summary: The group works on reinforcement learning and multi-agent RL, including conservative offline MARL, reward-machine transfer and learned multi-agent pathfinding, and LLM-based agents.
question: How can teams of learning agents coordinate and transfer knowledge across tasks?

name: Xiaolong Wang group
institution: UC San Diego; Meta Superintelligence Labs
summary: Builds world models and RL methods for continuous control and dexterous/humanoid robots.
question: How can embodied agents learn general skills from world models and large-scale data?

name: Xingyu Zhou group (Xingyu Zhou)
summary: The group develops reinforcement learning and alignment algorithms with privacy and robustness guarantees.
question: How can reinforcement learning and alignment protect user privacy while staying robust and efficient?

name: Xue Bin (Jason) Peng group (Xue Bin Peng)
primary: RL for character and humanoid motion
summary: The group works at the intersection of computer graphics and machine learning, using reinforcement learning for motion control of simulated characters and humanoid robots.
question: How can reinforcement learning produce natural, versatile motor skills for simulated characters and robots?

name: Xuezhou Zhang group (Xuezhou Zhang)
summary: The group studies reinforcement learning theory, RLHF exploration and adversarial reward poisoning, and RL methods for language-model reasoning.
question: How can reinforcement learning remain efficient and secure when rewards are learned or manipulated?

name: Yang Gao group (Yang Gao)
institution: Tsinghua University (IIIS); Shanghai Qi Zhi Institute
summary: The group combines computer vision priors with robot learning, including reward learning from videos and online imitation and RL for manipulation and humanoid control.
question: How can prior knowledge from computer vision make robot manipulation learning more efficient and effective?

name: Yi Wu group (Yi Wu)
institution: Tsinghua University (IIIS); Shanghai Qi Zhi Institute
summary: The group develops multi-agent and large-scale distributed RL algorithms and systems, including the AReaL asynchronous RL system for language-model reasoning, and applies RL to robot control.
question: How can deep and multi-agent reinforcement learning be scaled to large distributed systems and complex agents?

name: Yingbin Liang group
summary: Develops provably efficient reinforcement learning algorithms and analyses RL training dynamics, including actor-critic for low-rank MDPs and RL with verifiable rewards.
question: What makes reinforcement learning algorithms provably efficient, and how do their training dynamics behave?

name: Yishay Mansour group
summary: The group studies computational learning theory for Markov decision processes, bandits and online learning, including regret and sample-complexity bounds for policy optimization.
question: What are the statistical and computational limits of learning to act in Markov decision processes and online decision problems?

name: Youngchul Sung group (Youngchul Sung)
summary: The group develops reinforcement learning algorithms for multi-objective, constrained and multi-task settings and flow-matching actor-critic methods for offline and offline-to-online RL.
question: How can agents learn policies that balance several objectives and constraints from limited or offline data?

name: Yuanyuan Shi group (Yuanyuan Shi)
primary: RL for control and energy systems
summary: The group combines reinforcement learning and control theory for safe learning-based control, with applications in energy systems.
question: How can learning-based controllers be made safe and stable for physical systems?

name: Yue Wang group (Yue Wang)
institution: University of Central Florida (Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering)
summary: The group studies distributionally robust reinforcement learning, including robust average-reward MDPs, robust Markov games and model-free robust algorithms with sample-complexity guarantees.
question: How can reinforcement learning policies remain reliable when the deployment environment differs from the training model?

name: Yuejie Chi group
primary: RL theory and RL for LLMs
summary: Studies theoretical and algorithmic foundations of reinforcement learning, including sample-efficient RL and the learning dynamics of RL for language models.
question: What are the statistical and computational limits of reinforcement learning, and how can algorithms reach them?

name: Yunbo Wang group (Yunbo Wang)
institution: Shanghai Jiao Tong University (Artificial Intelligence Institute, School of Computer Science)
summary: The group studies world models and model-based reinforcement learning for embodied agents, including video-enhanced offline RL, open-world imagination-based RL and humanoid locomotion.
question: How can embodied agents use learned world models and imagination to make decisions that generalise across open-world scenarios?

name: Yuting Wei group (Yuting Wei)
institution: University of Pennsylvania (Wharton Statistics and Data Science)
summary: The group studies the statistical theory of reinforcement learning, including inference for TD learning and sample-optimal actor-critic methods.
question: What are the statistical limits of policy evaluation and policy learning in reinforcement learning?

name: Yuxin Chen group (Yuxin Chen)
institution: University of Pennsylvania (Wharton Statistics and Data Science)
summary: The group develops statistical and optimisation theory for reinforcement learning, including minimax regret, reward-free exploration and RLVR dynamics.
question: How many samples does reinforcement learning fundamentally need, and which algorithms attain that limit?

name: Zeb Kurth-Nelson (Max Planck UCL Centre)
institution: Max Planck UCL Centre for Computational Psychiatry and Ageing Research, University College London
primary: replay and RL in the brain
topics: deep rl models of the brain
summary: Studies neural replay, credit assignment and distributional reward coding in humans using models inspired by deep RL.
question: How do deep RL principles, exploration and spontaneous replay sequences account for decision making in the brain?

name: Zenke Lab (Friedemann Zenke)
institution: Friedrich Miescher Institute for Biomedical Research
summary: Computational neuroscience lab that develops reconstruction-free world models for model-based RL and planning alongside work on biologically plausible learning.
question: How do neural circuits learn predictive representations of the world that support planning and control?

name: Zhaoran Wang group
primary: RL theory and RL for LLMs
summary: Works on theoretical foundations of deep reinforcement learning and multi-agent decision making, and on RL methods for language-model reasoning.
question: How can data-driven decision-making methods be made provably efficient?

name: Zhengyuan Zhou group (Zhengyuan Zhou)
institution: New York University (Stern School of Business)
summary: The group studies data-driven decision making, including distributionally robust and concurrent reinforcement learning and bandits for operations.
question: How can decision policies learned from data remain robust in operational settings?

name: Zhiguang Cao group (Zhiguang Cao)
summary: The group uses deep reinforcement learning and related learning methods to solve combinatorial optimisation problems such as vehicle routing and scheduling.
question: How can deep reinforcement learning learn solvers for hard combinatorial optimisation problems?

name: Zhuoran Yang group
summary: Develops statistical and optimization theory for reinforcement learning, especially multi-agent settings with strategic interaction, offline RL and in-context RL.
question: What are the theoretical foundations of reinforcement learning when multiple agents interact strategically?

name: Zongqing Lu group (Zongqing Lu)
institution: Peking University (School of Computer Science); BeingBeyond
primary: RL for embodied agents and humanoids
summary: The group studies reinforcement learning, multimodal models and general agents so that robots and agents can acquire skills, cooperate and communicate in open worlds.
question: How can robots and agents autonomously acquire skills to accomplish tasks, cooperate and communicate in the open world?

name: Zongzhang Zhang group (Zongzhang Zhang)
institution: Nanjing University (LAMDA; School of Artificial Intelligence)
summary: The group studies deep and multi-agent RL, reward models for RL, and online RL for safety-critical settings such as autonomous driving.
question: How can reward design, coordination and online adaptation make deep reinforcement learning reliable in multi-agent and safety-critical settings?

name: Özgür Şimşek (University of Bath)
summary: Works on RL foundations including explanations of RL agents with Shapley values and learning distance-based state representations.
question: How can reinforcement-learning agents be understood, explained and made to act well under bounded rationality?
